body: The event listener on the helper should be removed on `dispose`.
Would be nice to have the return type, we should enforce this `tslint` rule.

We could use directly `name`. For a `NumericRefinement` it's the `string` representation of the `numericValue`.

https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/be22f0624b2714334c95cbee8a1b75115a6273b2/src/lib/utils/getRefinements.ts#L138-L139
Why not call `onHelperChange` since it's already bounded to the correct params?
Good point, I forgot to refactor this!
Yes, I see the value now!
Good point, probably not. Will update.
isn't the return type usually inferred?
It is, but you can see it as a contract for the implementation of the function. If you were to return some other type, you can spot the error quickly.
@Haroenv Yes it is, but it's easier to follow the code with the argument + return type.

I didn't understood your point. 

The only difference is that the return type of the map is an array of string.

Yes, which means that the `trackedFilters` functions will get called with strings, even for numeric refinements.

Example:

```js
queryRuleContext({
  price: (values: string[]) => values, // note that prices are now strings
})
```

I think it's a bit misleading because in this example prices are numeric in the records. WDYT?
You can keep as is. Note that values are stringified anyway once we send them.
